_about: Moments and literature transition temperatures for the four cases of Table IV. Every lambda is a literature value; every M is our own digitized estimate of lambda * <omega^2>, derived from the Eliashberg functions of the cited papers as described in LitConventional.md and LitHydrides.md. No numerical alpha^2F array is deposited with this archive; the records state the integrations and the arithmetic that produced each M.

cases.label: Pb
sources: Savrasov & Savrasov, Phys. Rev. B 54, 16487 (1996), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.54.16487: lambda, the Eliashberg-solution Tc 7.19 K and the McMillan 6.81 K
cases.caveat: measured Tc is taken from the tabulated Eliashberg/McMillan entries of the cited paper, whose primary Tc source is not specified there; M carries an indicative 10 percent digitization uncertainty

cases.label: Nb
sources: Savrasov & Savrasov, Phys. Rev. B 54, 16487 (1996), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.54.16487: lambda and the Eliashberg-solution Tc 9.25 K
cases.caveat: as for Pb, with the same 10 percent indicative uncertainty in M

cases.label: MgB2
sources: Choi et al., Phys. Rev. B 66, 020513 (2002), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.66.020513: lambda 0.61 and omega_log 63.5 meV for the anharmonic spectrum
Nagamatsu et al., Nature 410, 63 (2001), doi:10.1038/35065039: measured Tc 39 K
cases.caveat: the digitized reference spectrum is isotropic while the material is strongly anisotropic (the same coupling gives 19 K isotropic and 39 K anisotropic in the cited isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg calculation), so the ratio is against an isotropic reference only; M carries an indicative 5 percent uncertainty
cases.note_recomputed: the C-LAMBDA release record prints 113.504 K for this entry; exact recomputation with the same inputs and constants gives 113.5065 K, an arithmetic slip of 0.002 K, far inside the stated 5 percent uncertainty in M. The manuscript prints the recomputed 113.51 K.

cases.label: LaH10, 129 GPa
cases.pressures: the density-functional spectrum is at 129 GPa; the measured points are at 145 and 135 GPa
sources: Errea et al., Nature 578, 66 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41586-020-1955-z: calculated lambda 3.62 and omega_log 76.4 meV at 129 GPa (Extended Data Table I)
Drozdov et al., Nature 569, 528 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1201-8: measured ~245 K at 135 GPa and ~244 K at 145 GPa (Fig. 1 caption and text)
digitization note LitHydrides.md: M = 3.62 * (0.10086)^2 from a vector digitization of the plotted alpha^2F (Extended Data Fig. 4)
cases.caveat: the density-functional pressure and the measured pressures do not coincide, so the ratio mixes two pressures; M carries an indicative 5 percent uncertainty; the measured points are literature values and their Tc criterion is not stated as onset or midpoint in the cited figure
cases.note_recomputed: 244 K over 367.1821 K is 0.66452, which rounds to 0.665; an earlier draft truncated it to 0.664.
